items.title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $φ^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
items.summary: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states.

items.title: Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling
items.summary: Boson sampling machines have become a fruitful tool for establishing new concepts, which connect fundamental physics with computer science applications. Here, we exploit the intrinsically high-dimensional correlations generated by the measurement outcomes of a multiphoton boson sampling machine and demonstrate how a reconfigurable architecture can be programmed to autonomously model the time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems that describe complex fluid flows.

items.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
items.summary: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. The full stack of quantum computing encompasses several tasks: preparation of logical code states, implementation of logical gates, logical routines on encoded qubits, etc.

items.title: Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability
items.summary: Whether local reduced states are compatible with a global quantum state---the quantum marginal problem---is central to quantum information and simulation. Here we present a solution to the ensemble marginal problem for qubits based on the representability theory of fermions.

items.title: Dissipation as a Resource for Entanglement via High-Spin Mediator Purification
items.summary: We study entanglement generation between two spin qubits mediated by a single, thermally mixed, high-spin ($S=5/2$) magnetic impurity, using the Lindblad master equation to compare coherent and dissipative control of the mediator. We show that no coherent drive, however strong or resonant, can purify the mediator beyond its thermal value --- a direct consequence of unitary evolution exactly preserving state purity --- while a dissipative channel purifies it up to the limit set by the optical pumping cycle itself,…

items.title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
items.summary: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes.

items.title: Symmetry-Controlled Quantum State Transfer in Poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene: From Heisenberg to Hubbard Dynamics
items.summary: We investigate quantum state transfer in the poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene lattice using isotropic Heisenberg and Hubbard models. For a 16-site lattice, reflection symmetry separates the single-excitation Hamiltonian into independent triplet and singlet sectors, allowing analytical determination of the energy spectra.

items.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
items.summary: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable.

items.title: Nesting in additive manufacturing using quantum annealing
items.summary: Nesting in powder bed fusion (PBF), an additive manufacturing (AM) process, determines the positions and orientations of parts within the build space and influences build height and build time. As the number of parts and feasible placements increases, the nesting problem becomes computationally demanding.

items.title: Tessa: Encoding Classical Data Across an Entire Quantum Processor
items.summary: We present Tessa, a hardware-aware, device-wide scheme to encode classical data on quantum computers. We use it to experimentally encode and decode up to $1568$ real values using IBM's Phoenix and Fez quantum computers on a variety of data.

items.title: Entanglement and information dynamics in charged dual-unitary circuits with impurities
items.summary: Local parts of a closed, non-equilibrium quantum many-body system can reach stationarity through the buildup of entanglement between different regions. In this paper we investigate how this process is affected by the presence of a quantum impurity that breaks a global symmetry of the bulk.

items.title: Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
items.summary: Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics. For infinite systems, however, MPS algorithms, the standard classical reference in one dimension, conventionally rely on a computational compromise: replacing these interactions by fitted sums of exponentials.

items.title: Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
items.summary: Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay $t_{\mathrm{SR}}$ and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number $N$. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate.

items.title: Quantum computational spectroscopy of complex resonances and optical residues
items.summary: Optical spectra of dissipative molecular systems depend on both complex resonance energies and the way each resonance couples to an optical probe. In a non-Hermitian description, these con- tributions are determined by complex residues involving left and right eigenvectors.

items.title: Structure makes quantum circuits trainable
items.summary: The scalability of variational quantum algorithms is limited by barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in system size. This worst-case result raises fundamental questions about the trainability of quantum AI models.

items.title: Efficient Parameter Estimation through Quantum Extreme Learning
items.summary: Quantum sensing protocols rely on the efficient processing of measurement outcomes to infer unknown physical parameters. Conventional optimal estimators, such as Bayesian inference and maximum likelihood estimation, require to construct a likelihood function whose efficient classical construction requires full knowledge of the dynamics, which may practically be infeasible.

items.title: Quantum thermometry with k-local Hamiltonians
items.summary: In equilibrium quantum thermometry, the precision of temperature estimation increases with the heat capacity of the probe thermometer. For an n-body thermometer, the maximum heat capacity is attained by a Hamiltonian that requires n-local interactions, making its physical implementation challenging.

items.title: Formulating Uncomputation Beyond Classical Ancilla Use
items.summary: Ancilla qubits are routinely used to simplify quantum circuit construction and reduce implementation costs, but their use introduces the burden of designing proper uncomputation afterward. To alleviate this, prior work has developed automated uncomputation synthesis based on a computational-basis formulation of ancilla use.

items.title: Chip-Based Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution with Uncertainty-Principle-Based Composable Security
items.summary: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution offers a promising platform for scalable quantum networks through its compatibility with standard telecommunications technology and photonic integration. High-order discrete modulation facilitates practical implementation while approaching the key-rate performance of ideal Gaussian modulation, but its finite-size composable security analysis entails substantial computational overhead.

items.title: Observing Enhanced Entanglement in an Ising Quantum Register Beyond Weak Measurement
items.summary: Measurements often yield a disentangled quantum state which is the most probable measurement outcome while the measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement could be exponentially less probable or absent. Higher probability in measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement is virtue in experimental observation of enhance entanglement in post-selected or Born-rule measurements with less resources in noisy quantum devices.

items.title: Fer expansion converges almost twice as far as Magnus for qubits
items.summary: The Fer expansion writes the propagator of a time-dependent Hamiltonian as a product of unitary exponentials whose error decreases doubly exponentially with the number of factors, while the Magnus expansion improves by one order at a time. Its convergence, however, was guaranteed only below a radius of about $2.6058$, smaller than the Magnus radius $π$.

items.title: An Incomplete-Preference Quantum Anscombe--Aumann Representation
items.summary: This work develops a generalised Anscombe--Aumann framework in which acts map a finite set of states of the world into the effect interval of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, while preferences need not be complete. The construction keeps three logically distinct questions separate.

items.title: Maximally Entangled Mutually Unbiased Bases in Bipartite Systems of Unequal Prime Dimensions
items.summary: Mutually unbiased bases with prescribed entanglement properties are of fundamental interest in quantum information theory. In the interesting case of a bipartite Hilbert space of unequal prime dimensions, $\mathcal{H}_p\otimes\mathcal{H}_q$, with $p<q$ prime, the standard solution provides $p+1$ product bases.

items.title: Spin Interferometry Generated by Cavity Memory
items.summary: We report the control and observation of coherent spin interferometry generated by cavity memory using an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers coupled to a microwave cavity. The abrupt switch-on and switch-off of a detuned drive produce transient fields at the cavity frequency that supply the two spin rotations for Ramsey interferometry, observed using both microwave and fluorescence readout.

items.title: Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors
items.summary: The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a $[[4,1]]$ code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a $256\times 256$ Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases.

items.title: Quantum tomography of Higgsstrahlung: Higgs boson self-coupling and $Z$ boson anomalous couplings
items.summary: The Higgs boson self-coupling enters the Higgsstrahlung process $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at one loop. The three diagrams that carry it project onto two Lorentz structures: the tree-level one, which rescales the rate, and that of the CP-even anomalous coupling $b_Z$, which changes the polarization of the final-state $Z$ boson.

items.title: Quantum Preparation without Disturbance: Information Costs and Hypothesis Testing
items.summary: We determine the minimum information cost of preparing either of two quantum states with one common device while preserving its memory. Measured by the Umegaki relative entropy between the two possible memory states, this minimum is the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy of the target states.

items.title: Quantum phase estimation on a Rydberg quantum simulator
items.summary: Determining the energy spectrum of a many-body quantum system is a central goal of quantum physics. Ground-state energies underpin materials science and quantum chemistry, whereas excited states govern dynamical phenomena such as quantum thermalization.

items.title: Efficient Iterative Symmetrization algorithm for quantum computing and hadron applications
items.summary: Efficient algorithms for the (anti)symmetrization of quantum registers are necessary for upcoming few- and many-body physics applications, from atomic to particle-physics scales. We propose a recursive algorithm (anti)symmetrizing the last particle added to memory, each time one is created or destroyed, respect to the rest of already (anti)symmetrized ones.

items.title: Hybrid Krotov gradient descent Optimization for Quantum Machine Learning
items.summary: We introduce and study a Krotov-inspired discrete adjoint optimization scheme for quantum machine learning and focus on a hybrid online-to-batch schedule. The method transfers the forward/costate/local-update logic of continuous-time optimal control to parameterized quantum circuits by replacing time locality with gate-index locality.

items.title: Linear-optical generation of approximate higher-component cat states
items.summary: We propose a method for generating higher-component cat states by interfering two $N$-component cat states on a half beam splitter and measuring one output with a photon-number-resolving detector. The Fock components of the conditional output are restricted to a single residue class modulo $2N$.

items.title: Hidden Quantum Markov Processes: Mealy Formulation and Observable Reduction
items.summary: We formulate hidden quantum Markov processes in a Mealy architecture using a single completely positive unital transition expectation coupling the present hidden system, the emitted output, and the next hidden system. Together with a boundary state, it generates a quasi-local, finitely correlated hidden--output state; for the commutative generator associated with a classical Mealy kernel, this state is the full joint law of the classical Mealy model.

items.title: Quantum kinetic uncertainty relations: Role of coherence in current fluctuation bounds
items.summary: We present a comparative analysis of three quantum versions of the kinetic uncertainty relation (KUR), which incorporate coherence-dependent corrections to the classical bound. Using a three-level maser heat engine as a paradigmatic quantum thermal machine, we identify the operating regimes in which each formulation provides the tightest constraint on current fluctuations.

items.title: Max-Cut QAOA on Non-Hardware-Native Graphs via MinLA Surrogates and Configuration Recovery
items.summary: For non-hardware-native \textsc{MAX-CUT} instances, the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can incur additional two-qubit depth overhead due to SWAP-based routing of interactions between non-adjacent qubits. We propose a hybrid quantum--classical workflow that reduces this depth by selectively removing interactions and subsequently recovers solution quality through classical optimization of the original \textsc{MAX-CUT} objective.

items.title: The cone of states over time: exact tests and convergent two-sided hierarchies
items.summary: A state over time (stote) pairs a state $ρ$ with a channel $\mathcal{E}$ as the Hermitian, generally non-positive operator $(ρ\otimes\mathbf{1})\star J_\mathcal{E}$. We study the convex cone $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ generated by these operators.

items.title: A Concise Introduction to Quantum Electromagnetics
items.summary: This book introduces quantum electromagnetics to readers trained in classical electromagnetics, without assuming a systematic background in quantum mechanics. The central question is when classical descriptions suffice, and when the quantum states of matter or the field must be retained explicitly.

items.title: The Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment: classical and quantum optimization approaches
items.summary: Efficient railway rolling stock management requires the coordinated planning of train-unit assignment, shunting movements, track occupation, service operations, and workforce allocation. These interdependent decisions give rise to a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly as the size of the fleet and the planning horizon increase.

items.title: Digital Coherent Twin-Field Quantum Key Distribution with Gaussian-Modulated Coherent States
items.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables information-theoretically secure key sharing between two distant parties. Recently, one promising QKD protocol which can distribute a secret key over long distances called twin-field QKD (TF-QKD) has been developed.

items.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
items.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde ρ$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}ψ=Eψ$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $Σ:=\inf\mathop{\rm ess.spec} (H_{N,Z})$, then \[ \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde ρ(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetildeρ(r)} =-2α_0, \] with $α_0=\sup\{α\ge…

items.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
items.summary: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound.

items.title: Efficient representations by PEPS: critical free-fermion and chiral topological states
items.summary: We construct projected entangled-pair state (PEPS) approximations to various many-body states in 2D lattices with global error at most $ε$ and bond dimension polynomial in the system size and $1/ε$. They include critical free-fermion models in two dimensions, as well as chiral topological states.

items.title: Dissipation-induced integrability in a spin-1 chain and a Bose-Hubbard mixture
items.summary: We construct a nonintegrable spin-1 chain that acquires a Yang--Baxter integrable no-jump Hamiltonian through a single dissipative channel per bond. Energy is the only nontrivial finite-range charge of the isolated periodic bulk.

items.title: Hybrid Uncertainty in the Real Forms of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)$
items.summary: An optimized commutator bound can lie strictly below the quantum infimum even when its minimizing mean is realized by a quantum state. We study hybrid uncertainty, defined as the sum of pairwise products of standard deviations.

items.title: Underlying orbital U(1) symmetry in quantum limit cycles
items.summary: Quantum limit cycles exhibit harmonic Liouvillian spectra, yet their underlying orbital $U(1)$ structure is not generally explicit in the absence of physical rotational symmetry. Here, we construct a unitary representation of orbital phase translations through a similarity transformation that maps the harmonic nondecaying Liouvillian sector onto a Hermitian angular-momentum Hamiltonian.

items.title: Hardware-aware sampling and QPU-informed Monte Carlo with quantum annealers
items.summary: We study how the physical representation of a logical model affects sampling by quantum annealers and its use in corrected Monte Carlo. The square-lattice Ising model provides controlled classical references.

items.title: Four-Sector Propagation-Trapping Decomposition and Inverse Design of Initial States in Grover-Coined Quantum Walks on Multiedge Path Graphs
items.summary: Controlling propagation and trapping through initial-state preparation requires an explicit relation between the initial amplitudes and the corresponding directional probabilities. We establish this relation for a discrete-time Grover-coined quantum walk on a multiedge path graph with even degree d = 2M, where M is at least 2, and two equal directional blocks.

items.title: Reference-Assisted Qutrit Control and Conditional One-Round Distillation in a Charge-4e Superconductor Model
items.summary: We formulate a charge-$4e$ parafermionic-vortex route to qutrit processing as a conditional theory with explicit operational assumptions. Sector preservation and same-label charge-conjugation covariance imply closure for every adaptive visible record.

items.title: Local gluing classification and bulk-locked clock rings for $\mathbb{Z}_N$ models on a Klein bottle
items.summary: We classify local reflection gluings of the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ plaquette model on lattice Klein bottles and solve the obstructed literal seam. Within the monomial far-corner ansatz, all commuting gluings form a family labelled by a unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}_N$.

items.title: No universal LOCC entanglement purification
items.summary: Entanglement purification aims to obtain high-fidelity entangled states from noisy entangled states. This task becomes particularly challenging when the available input states are finite in number, only partially characterized, and may not be identical.

items.title: Tight Quantum Query Bounds for Collision Finding over Arbitrary Bounded Types
items.summary: We determine the bounded-error quantum query complexity of finding one $r$-collision in an $N$-input function of prescribed type, which specifies all equality-class sizes. For every fixed maximum class size and collision order, we give a tight bound as the maximum of scales determined by the numbers of classes of size at least $2,\ldots,r$.

items.title: Compiling Matrix Formulas to Quantum Block Encodings
items.summary: Realizing the promise of quantum applications such as chemistry or fluid dynamics requires building quantum circuits that efficiently encode and manipulate exponentially large matrices. This process forces researchers to grapple with the reality that a matrix expressible as one equation on paper can map to thousands of bit-level quantum logic gates, historically written by hand.

items.title: Multitime Equilibration and Multitime Mpemba Effects
items.summary: Equilibration of a quantum state leaves open whether its response to later interventions has also equilibrated. We establish multitime equilibration for a continuous process on a fixed observation window, retaining the autonomous system--environment dynamics and all internal time differences.

items.title: Fast forward-and-backward creation of non-equilibrium Gibbs state in driven dissipative quantum systems
items.summary: We present the fast-forward (FF) approach to adiabatic time evolution of an open dissipative quantum system within the framework of the Gorini-Kosaakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) equation. Taking a harmonic oscillator (HO) and a quantum spin as prototype systems under a rapid change of the driving field and in contact with the heat reservoir, we reveal the protocol which creates the non-equilibrium Gibbs state.

items.title: Quantum Data Processing Unit for Neutral-Atom Quantum Computers
items.summary: Quantum computers need real-time classical processing to convert measurement data into feedback within device-specific timing constraints. We introduce the quantum data processing unit (QDPU), an architecture between a quantum device and its controller.

items.title: Linear monitoring-feedback Model for Linearized gravity
items.summary: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics.

items.title: Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
items.summary: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling $f=n/L$ except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms.

items.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life
items.summary: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes. A previous digital-life framework distinguishes online (busy) and offline (idle) channels, but leaves open whether these are separate programs or phases of a common process and how their operations should be ordered.

items.title: A systems-level energetic framework for conscious processing: energetic organization as a constraint on large-scale neural integration
items.summary: Conscious processing is associated with coordinated interactions among distributed neural systems, yet the biological constraints that enable and sustain large-scale neural integration remain incompletely understood. Contemporary theories emphasize computational, informational, and network mechanisms, while the potential contribution of systems-level energetic organization has received comparatively less explicit theoretical attention.

items.title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
items.summary: In the present paper we study the formulation of a search problem and the efficiency of multi-particle quantum walk search algorithms. The discrete-time evolution of each particle in space is treated according to Grover's quantum walk evolution operator.

items.title: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: A Wave Packet Approach in Neutrino Oscillation with Matter
items.summary: In this work, we investigate quantum correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations beyond the standard plane-wave (PW) description by employing a wave-packet formalism in the presence of constant matter density. We study three quantum correlation measures, namely the residual $l_1$-norm coherence, Concurrence Fill, and Three-$π$ entanglement, and express them in terms of transition probabilities for an initial muon-flavor state.

items.title: DRAG-Inspired Single Flux Quantum Control of Superconducting Qubits
items.summary: Scalable control remains a major challenge for superconducting quantum processors due to the wiring, thermal load, and hardware complexity associated with conventional microwave-based architectures. A framework for qubit control based on Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) digital electronics is presented.

items.title: Note on quantum optimal measurements of CMB spectral distortions
items.summary: As quantum sensing techniques continue to push the frontier of detection of ultra-weak signals, one may wonder if a sophisticated quantum strategy could be used to enable measurement of spectral distortions in the cosmic microwave background. Using quantum Fisher information techniques, we prove that the optimal strategy is simple frequency-binned intensity measurement.

items.title: Recursive Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz
items.summary: The recursive quantum approximate optimisation algorithm~(RQAOA) shrinks an unconstrained combinatorial optimisation problem by eliminating one variable at a time, guided by correlations measured in variational quantum states. We extend this recursion to constrained problems by building on the quantum alternating operator ansatz, which restricts the evolution to feasible solutions through a feasible initial state and feasibility-preserving mixers.

items.title: Finite-time spectral enhancement of transient quantum thermometry
items.summary: Transient quantum thermometry extracts temperature information before a probe reaches thermal equilibrium. We study how finite interaction times affect thermometric precision for a harmonic-oscillator probe prepared in a number state and weakly coupled to a thermal bosonic reservoir.

items.title: Probing Spatiotemporal Quantum Correlations with Two-Qubit Relaxometry
items.summary: Quantum impurities and spin qubits are powerful local probes of magnetic fluctuations, but conventional relaxometry reduces their information to a local relaxation rate at a single frequency. Building on advances in two-qubit sensing of spatial correlations, we show how two complementary protocols probe finite-time correlations in interacting quantum matter.

items.title: The radical pair mechanism can generate nuclear-spin entanglement
items.summary: The radical pair mechanism is a quantum-mechanical process underlying weak magnetic field effects in chemical and biological systems. While nuclear polarization and electronic entanglement in this mechanism have been studied extensively, the possibility of creating entanglement between nuclear spins has, to the best of our knowledge, remained unexplored.

items.title: Efficient quantum-circuit simulation of classical control of computational order
items.summary: We show that quantum circuits with classical control of computational order admit an efficient simulation by fixed-order quantum circuits: any such transformation acting on $N$ independent quantum channels can be deterministically, exactly, and universally simulated using at most $N^2$ queries. We generalize these constructions to extended, bipartite quantum channels and quantum instruments, and demonstrate that they can be implemented catalytically, without consuming the additional $N^2-N$ queries required for…

items.title: Optically-induced electric Aharonov-Bohm effect
items.summary: Although it was proposed almost 70 years ago, the electric version of the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect, where the interference pattern of quantum charged particles is affected by electric fields that do not interact locally with them, was never experimentally implemented. Here we propose a feasible way to experimentally verify such an important effect, for an electron double-slit interferometer with the slits carved in a nonlinear crystal.

items.title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
items.summary: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications.

items.title: Analytic spread complexity in three-level systems and the spacing-ratio distribution
items.summary: The spread complexity characterizes the spreading of a quantum state over the Krylov basis and has been proposed to capture the correlations between energy levels. How such correlations manifest in the dynamics has been studied mainly numerically for large matrices.

items.title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
items.summary: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response.

items.title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
items.summary: The universal properties of state ensembles generated by quantum dynamics provide a refined lens into Hilbert-space ergodicity and deep thermalisation, or lack thereof. We investigate deep-ergodicity breaking transitions of an ancillary qubit entangled with a system undergoing dynamics via hybrid quantum circuits, where unitary evolution is interspersed with projective measurements.

items.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
items.summary: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $Λ$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation.

items.title: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
items.summary: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions.

items.title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation
items.summary: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time.

items.title: Attention Renders Sensory Contents into Conscious State via Content-invariant Frontal-Posterior Coupling in Humans
items.summary: Abstract Although attention promotes conscious perception, how it does so remains unclear. Human neuroimaging research has richly characterized attentional modulation upon visual processing, yet it remains unclear which of its components act as precursors of consciousness, which constitute consciousness itself, and which merely reflect post-perceptual, response-related operations.

items.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
items.summary: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. In standard bedside assessments, these stimuli are applied manually, resulting in substantial variation in force, duration, frequency, and location.

items.title: Digital Minds: Issues in the Philosophy of Mind and Cognitive Science
items.summary: ABSTRACT This article provides a contemporary introduction to issues in the philosophy of mind and cognitive science that are studied within the emerging field of digital minds research. We explore the potential for AI systems to have mental states.

items.title: Local enhancement of finite-strength code preparation: recoverability and Wilson coherence
items.summary: Stabilizer measurements provide a direct route to preparing quantum error-correcting codes and long-range entangled states. In realistic implementations, however, finite measurement strength can coherently deform the encoding map away from the projective limit.

items.title: Probing chaos and criticality with observational entropy and finite-resolution measurements
items.summary: Coarse-grained measurements offer a scalable alternative to full state tomography for characterizing complex quantum dynamics. We show that observational entropy (OE), an information-theoretic entropy defined directly from finite-resolution measurement outcomes, provides a unified and experimentally accessible framework for quantifying chaos and probing criticality.

items.title: Quantum resources for everlasting communication security
items.summary: Abstract Quantum cryptography provides communication with everlasting security—a property unattainable by classical or post-quantum cryptography. Traditionally, quantum cryptography proclaims everlasting security by relying on principles such as no-cloning theorem, Bell inequalities, or the uncertainty principle, along with the standard assumption that legitimate users have no control over the communication channel.

items.title: The quantum-ready college: quantum technologies as an industry shift and how higher education should prepare
items.summary: Purpose This paper examines the emerging industry shift in which quantum technologies are evolving from isolated scientific breakthroughs into full-scale innovation ecosystems that will reshape higher education. Its purpose is to demonstrate why colleges must prepare now, well before fault tolerant quantum computers arrive, by developing quantum ready capacities across curriculum, workforce development, partnerships and cybersecurity.

items.title: Quantum Searching and Optimization Algorithms: A Comprehensive Guide
items.summary: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information processing. It begins by establishing the conceptual and mathematical foundations of quantum computation, including quantum gates, circuit design, quantum parallelism, and the distinctions between classical and quantum models of information processing.

items.title: Unitarity with respect to the clock of a dynamical local observer and the Einstein equivalence principle
items.summary: We investigate the unitarity of quantum evolution relative to an internal time defined by a local observer's clock. The observer is modeled as a relativistic particle carrying both a clock and a matter-field detector, analyzed first on a fixed curved background and subsequently within a fully diffeomorphism-invariant theory of dynamical gravity.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics of Local Anesthetics in Fascial Plane Blocks: Clinical Implications and Safety Considerations-A Narrative Review
items.summary: Fascial plane blocks (FPBs) are increasingly used in modern regional anaesthesia and differ from conventional nerve blocks by delivering local anesthetic (LA) into interfascial compartments. This approach results in distinct pharmacokinetics with clinically relevant systemic absorption.

items.summary: Quantum computers provide a promising platform to understand and control the dynamics of quantum many-body systems, yet current devices operate in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) regime, where decoherence caused by interactions with the environment severely limit their ability to accurately carry out computations. This thesis investigates how these limitations affect the simulation of quantum many-body systems, and explores strategies to design efficient quantum algorithms that can operate under…

items.title: Multiparameter quantum estimation of circulant networks
items.summary: Networks provide a natural description of interaction patterns, transport media, and communication architectures. Accurately characterizing their coupling structure is a key challenge in quantum technologies.

items.title: Quantum-Assisted Generative Anomaly Detection: A Dimension-Controlled Study of Latent Refinement
items.summary: Anomaly-based malware detectors learn what benign files look like and flag deviations. Generative approaches to this problem can make use of a "latent" or "prior" data representation, which is often chosen to be a Gaussian distribution.

items.title: The Sociological Cogito and the Hard Problems of Science: Math, Logic, God, and Consciousness as Social Phenomena
items.summary: This groundbreaking work introduces the sociological cogito as a revolutionary paradigm for solving the most perplexing “hard problems” in science and philosophy: mathematics, logic, God, and consciousness. By challenging traditional Cartesian and Platonist approaches, it demonstrates how these seemingly transcendental phenomena are actually grounded in our social realities.

items.title: Illusionism as a theory of mental content
items.summary: Analytic philosophers of mind seemingly take the hard problem of consciousness to be the only aspect of the mind-body problem that has not been in principle solved. But phenomenal consciousness is not the only puzzling and mysterious mental phenomena.

items.title: Everettian chance in no uncertain terms
items.summary: Abstract The current landscape of views on the role of chance in the Everett interpretation is rocky. Everettians (Wallace, 2012; Sebens and Carroll, 2018; McQueen and Vaidman, 2019) agree that chance values should be derived using rules of rationality governing agents’ uncertain reasoning and/or decision-making, but they cannot agree on how.

items.title: The Hard Problem of Consciousness and Qualia in the Acta Universi Hypothesis
items.summary: The Hard Problem of Consciousness and Qualia in the Acta Universi Hypothesis Abstract (EN) The hard problem of consciousness asks why physical processes are accompanied by subjective experience. This paper offers a reformulation of the problem within the Acta Universi (AU) hypothesis—a speculative informational-entropic ontology.

items.title: A glutamatergic projection from the central medial thalamic nucleus to the red nucleus regulates states of consciousness during sevoflurane anesthesia in mice
items.summary: General anesthetics like sevoflurane are clinically essential, yet the neural circuits governing their induction of unconsciousness and recovery remain incompletely defined. Here, we show the potential involvement of the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (Vglut2)-expressing glutamatergic neurons in the central medial thalamus (CMT Vglut2 neurons) in modulation states of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia.

items.title: From unimodal to multimodal deep physiological signal analysis in healthcare: A survey of models, fusion and explainability
items.summary: Physiological signal analysis supports objective assessment of emotion, stress, pain, and disease progression in healthcare systems. Early research focused mainly on unimodal signals, which perform well in controlled settings but are often affected by noise, limited contextual information and reduced generalisability.

items.title: Patient-specific factors are associated with distinct brain network connectivity in disorders of consciousness
items.summary: Disorders of consciousness (DoC) arise from diverse etiologies and exhibit substantial clinical heterogeneity, including variations in patient age and time since injury. However, how these clinical characteristics relate to large-scale brain network connectivity and are associated with consciousness levels and functional outcomes remains poorly understood.

items.title: Spin-Based Quantum Information Processing in Cytoskeletal Filaments Using Nucleoside Phosphates
items.summary: Abstract Phosphorus nuclear spins are candidates for quantum information processing in biological matter because 31P is a spin-1/2nucleus without an electric quadrupole moment, although coherence remains environment-dependent. Recent work rangesfrom theoretical proposals based on phosphate ions and Posner molecules to experimental demonstrations of room-temperaturequantum logic in adenosine diphosphate.

items.title: Testing non-classical gravitational phase dynamics under strong dephasing
items.summary: Whether gravity must be quantum is often approached by asking whether two masses can become entangled through their mutual gravitational interaction. In practice, the weak interaction competes with environmental decoherence, so the final state may contain no entanglement even when the underlying gravitational phase remains coherent.

items.title: Quantum AI for E-Commerce: From Theory to Practice
items.summary: This book offers a multidisciplinary and business-focused exploration of AI and computing, highlighting their potential impact on digital commerce, entrepreneurship,and innovation. It critically examines the shift towards data-driven technologies as organisations strive to enhance value creation, operational efficiency, and customer experience.

items.title: Fixed-preparation short-time reconstruction of class-D BdG endpoint masses
items.summary: In one-dimensional class-D superconductors, the relative signs of the Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) masses at particle--hole-invariant momenta fix the bulk $\mathbb Z_2$ invariant. Band energies and transition-frequency peak locations alone cannot determine these signs.

items.title: Quantum Forensics in Cybercrime Investigation and Digital Forensics: From Digital Footprints to Strategic Decision-Making
items.summary: This paper proposes Quantum Forensics as a novel theoretical and applied paradigm for cybercrime investigation and digital forensics. The central thesis is that proving evidence in cyber crimes demands a dual approach: a quantitative, reproducible STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) method that demonstrates evidence significance scientifically, and an inferential method that connects facts to law through evidentiary frameworks spanning national legislation, international conventions, UNCITRAL…

items.title: Safety-First, Severity-Adapted Enhanced Recovery After Surgery for Patients with Neurodegenerative Disorders: A Narrative Review and Proposed Framework
items.summary: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways have been shown to improve perioperative outcomes in broad surgical populations. However, their safety, feasibility, and optimal adaptation remain uncertain in patients with neurodegenerative disorders (NDDs), particularly those with dementia and Parkinson's disease.

items.title: Distinguishing gagging, nausea, retching, and vomiting: A multidimensional psychophysiological framework
items.summary: Gagging, nausea, retching, and vomiting are often reported together clinically, but differ in their triggers, subjective features, motor organization, and relation to expulsion. This narrative review compares them using human studies, research on airway protection, and animal models of emesis.

items.title: Operationally induced preferred basis in unitary quantum mechanics
items.summary: Abstract The preferred-basis problem remains under unitary system–apparatus dynamics, whereas measurements have mutually exclusive outcomes. The present framework places basis selection in the complete preparation–measurement arrangement.

items.title: Universal quantum gate set for multimode Schrödinger cat states stabilized by nonlocal dissipation engineering
items.summary: Schrödinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multi-mode Schrödinger cat states as robust quantum memories, a framework for universal quantum computation has remained unavailable.

items.title: Anesthesia via Dissociative Overload: A Unified Theoretical Framework Linking DMT and Ketamine Through Sigma-1 Convergence, Entropic Saturation, and Workspace Flooding
items.summary: General anesthesia has long been understood as a unitary phenomenon driven by neural suppression — a reduction in cortical activity, entropy, and complexity that renders the brain unable to sustain conscious processing. Yet two structurally and pharmacologically distinct compounds, N,N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT) and ketamine, produce clinical unresponsiveness while maintaining or increasing cortical complexity, a pattern fundamentally incompatible with the suppression paradigm.

items.title: Nonlocality as a benchmarking tool for quantum processors
items.summary: Abstract Benchmarking quantum processors is a central task in every roadmap aimed at quantum advantage. Here, we discuss a benchmarking protocol based on the violation of the Svetlichny inequality, which is designed to simulate genuine multipartite nonlocality.
